quest.title: An Ark That Used to Be a Soul
quest.description: You must obtain the power that was separated from the Eye of Graeae so that the Eye can return and regain its body...

chapter.title: Her palace is collapsing into the Anemo and snow

talks.objective: Have a conversation on the train

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's so cold out there... The train's definitely much cozier...

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: That is precisely why the trains exist. Trekking long distances through such bitter cold would hardly be good for anyone's health.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: Perhaps that, too, was my creator's original purpose in establishing it... After all, this land of ice and snow is hardly a place fit for humans to survive.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Your creator...? Ah, could that be the strange woman we ran into earlier?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How rude! What do you mean, "strange woman"!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon definitely doesn't mean the strange woman you're talking about right now!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...You know, the one who appeared in that mumbly-jumbly town with the firebird, and in that castle full of Snegovik. Paimon remembers her name was Ak...

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: Miss Aksinya, yes. Judging from the memories I have recovered so far, she was once a member of the Belyi Tsar's research organization, the Aly{RUBY#[S]Hvergelmir}pium...

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: She created me so that I might... guide a certain mighty power, and create a "Tomorrow" — a world where no one would ever suffer again...

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: A land that has cast aside envy, hatred, and selfish desire. A "Courtyard of Carefree Light" held aloft by the hands of all living beings. Thus...

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: "Thus shall a radiant world descend, where there will be no distinction between human and human, nor between human and god."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A world where there's no distinction between humans and gods? Hmm... Paimon can't even imagine how you'd make that happen...

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: "A pure world of mankind, where gods need not wield divine power, and humans need not rely on gods."

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: ...That is the outcome of the plan, as I remember it.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: But as for how it was to be accomplished... I'm sorry, but I do not know the full scope of the final plan. To the plan as a whole, I was nothing more than a "tool" within it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon gets it! Goggles is like a crafting bench. It can craft all kinds of amazing things, but a crafting bench doesn't run around eating up its own materials.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: That is a very apt analogy. However, if I may, Miss Paimon, in present-day Snezhnaya, alchemy is not an officially supported field of study...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: R-Right... But, well, we're on our own train, so...

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: ...But should I reclaim my body? Once I do, that means I must complete my mission... "The Courtyard of Carefree Light"...

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: What if, after my memories are restored, I find that these are not the ones I wished to recover? What should I do then?

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: What if... What if that's the only reason I was created, the purpose I was destined for...?

choices.text: Then don't decide yet. Wait until you remember.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! It's definitely not good to decide when you don't know anything yet. No matter what, you've gotta remember everything first!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway... Goggles has helped us out a lot! Even if that wasn't what Goggles was originally created for, Goggles has still been really useful to us!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: When that time comes, just come back to us.

response.speaker: Eye of Graeae
response.text: ...Is that so?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Besides, we already talked about all the things we're going to do together when you get your body back! Warming up by the fire, having snowball fights, running around on the ice fields... We promised!

response.speaker: Eye of Graeae
response.text: Yes. I look forward to... adventuring together with you both after I recover my body.

response.speaker: Eye of Graeae
response.text: Though I have thought this countless times throughout our journey... I am truly glad that you were the one to bring me out of that place, and that I was able to meet you both.

response.speaker: Eye of Graeae
response.text: Let's go. It is time to go to the "Courtyard of Carefree Light," to the door that waits to be opened.

choices.text: What's wrong with a crafting bench wanting to craft!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Exactly! And if anyone's to blame, it's whoever misused the crafting bench!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wah, this is all your fault... Now Paimon can't stop imagining a crafting bench going "huff, huff" like some kind of dog!

talks.objective: Open the door leading to the Courtyard of Carefree Light

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: This is where the entrance to the Courtyard of Carefree Light is. Should I try to return my powers to this place and open the gate...?

response.speaker: Eye of Graeae
response.text: Let's perform the return ceremony then, and open the gate to the courtyard...

choices.text: No, let's come back to this later...

response.speaker: Eye of Graeae
response.text: Yes. It may be better to come back to this when you're more prepared.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're finally in. That felt really cold just now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We should be able to reconstruct Goggles' body, now right? ...Hold on, where's Goggles?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's going on!? Even those blue lenses have disappeared...

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: There is no cause for concern... The once-fragmented body, along with the consciousness bound to inanimate matter, have all returned to where they rightfully belong.

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: You may leave the Eye of Graeae in my keeping for a time. In my estimation, it is a form of homecoming for it anyhow.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A—Aksinya! It's you...!

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: Yes. I'm glad to see that you remember my name, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Goggles...

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: Don't worry, he will come to. Just maybe not so soon, that's all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, so he's getting his body back, right? Good as new? He'll be back to his original human form?

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: No, he will not. He will inhabit "another's form" and metamorphose into the true "Proto-Man." I suppose this might be slightly different from what you imagined.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hold on... This is all a little confusing. Didn't he want his old body back?

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: Not really.

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: He knows nothing because he has completely forgotten the past. To think that "reclaiming his old body" is the only thought driving him... Perhaps that in itself is a cruelty.

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: But reclaiming his old body was never his true purpose from the beginning. That was all merely preparation for assimilating into, and reforging, a form of an even higher order.

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: This is something he should come to comprehend once his memory is made whole.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Assimilating and being changed into a form of an even higher order..." Eh, are you saying that his body and powers will all go into someone else's body?

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: Yes, that would be right.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But how is that gonna happen when his body's already gone...?

choices.text: I see now. You're thinking of using Paimon's body.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? No way!!! But... hmm... if it's for Goggles, Paimon supposes she could make a little room for him...

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: Hahaha! I fear that assimilating him into Paimon's body will only bring about other complications.

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: #It isn't hard to piece together, {NICKNAME}. There is indeed a vessel left here at the Pale Crown Palace, where the old kings of Northland have been interred...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Are you talking about... the Belyi Tsar's body?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? The Belyi Tsar? But he's been dead for so many years! He can't be anything more than a pile of bones by now...

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: His Majesty is different. His body... has remained alive even after the passing of his consciousness.

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: Think of him as the "White Birch Tsar." In truth, we're speaking of what are the ever-growing 'nerves' of his husk, a shell that never truly perished, forever extending outward in longing. Hmm, the white birch... it scarcely resembles a tree, does it?

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: And five centuries on, His Majesty's body has yet to cease its longing...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What...? So the Belyi Tsar's body is still alive? After all this time??? But how can it be...?

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: You must admit, his existence is truly unique. Although he was not a Descender, he was of noble birth nevertheless. He was the culmination of Hyperborea's most advanced technologies, a being with a soul bestowed through nothing less than light itself...

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: The Hyperboreans even attempted to forge his body from the flesh and blood of the Primordial Cryo Dragon, just to give him authority equal to The One.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "He Who Came"? Who?

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: A will that was born alongside Teyvat, the master of the very first power of the Light Realm, and the King of all Dragon Lords: Nibelung.

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: Ever since his destruction, the place of Primordial Human, or Narayana, has sat vacant.

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: But in the heavens above, the cold blade of the master who must not be named... Ha, or should I say, that long nail of his... continued to hang high and pitiless over the world. And so...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: They... sought to create their own gods.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that's why they created the Belyi Tsar... But they couldn't possibly have called him that at the time. Did they call him the Primordial Human or something then?

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: Though they attempted to create the Primordial Human, the experiment went out of control. Otherwise, the Golden City would still be standing tall upon this land today... and where we stand would not have become this frozen expanse.

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: According to the record fragments we found inside the Shadow Realm, the corpse of the Cryo Dragon Sovereign and their unchecked authority turned the whole of Snezhnaya into the Holy Soil of primordial ice.

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: Even the ley lines in the area were affected, to the point that they became veins of pure crystal... That is, until He Who Came witnessed this and sent his heavenly nail crashing down.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ow... But um, since the experiment was a failure, how did the Belyi Tsar come about?

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: It spun out of control, but it was not a failure... A thousand years after that experiment and its cataclysmic impact finally cleared, His Majesty awoke from the remains of the Cryo Dragon.

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: However, his power was not fully complete, as the experiment was never brought to its conclusion... And by that time, Hyperborea had already sunk into the Shadow Realm, and the only ones seen in the land of ice and snow were the fae...

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: While most people believe the Belyi Tsar to be some kind of extraordinarily powerful fae, his true identity is far more noble...

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: The fact that the Hyperborea that had created him had already perished was one he could have easily left behind. But he chose to accept it... He accepted that he was the failed attempt of the Primordial Human project.

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: And that... included accepting all the responsibilities and consequences that came with it.

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: He was even willing to embrace humankind in this frozen land that swarmed with monsters, and he remained willing to... become the true Primordial Human.

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: This was a love, a grand and all-encompassing benevolence that we must never betray.

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: And Goggles... was the "Proto Man" that was created after countless experiments, and the Key that would allow His Majesty to become the Primordial Human.

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: This... is something that should have been started a long time ago. And now, it has become His Majesty's final wish...

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: #But thanks to the two of you, {NICKNAME} and Paimon, we can now complete his grand design.

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: Make no mistake, this is no light undertaking. It is an endeavor I had originally planned to spend twenty years completing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe! Paimon doesn't really get what you're talking about, but Paimon will happily accept your thanks anyway!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So what happens after...?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I mean, once the Primordial Human is complete...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, that's right! You keep talking about that "Courtyard of Carefree Light." What even is that place supposed to be...?

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: "Thus is the world of Aurion, the world of tomorrow... a realm that had cast aside envy, hatred, and selfish desire. All shall be able to love one another as in the very beginning, and this love shall be, in nature, everlasting."

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: "Thus shall a radiant world descend, where there will be no distinction between human and human, nor between human and god."

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: At least, that was the vision he described to us. But I understand it differently... The "love" he spoke of was simply a kind of spiritual overflow.

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: It's just that this overflow runs dry beneath the weight of countless sorrows. And so, those who once poured love begin to drain it from others, the selfless turn into hoarders, and trust is supplanted by fear and suspicion.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... Paimon doesn't get what you're saying at all...

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: Hmm. You are quite fond of eating, are you not, Paimon? Take the "Sweet Madame," for instance. You must have found it utterly delicious the very first time you tasted it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! Paimon even had two whole birds in one go!

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: Yes... But it did not taste quite as delicious the second time, did it? And by the third, the pleasure had faded even further... Eventually, a day will come when you find yourself completely sick of it altogether.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No way! Paimon will never get sick of eating Sweet Madame! Paimon knows for a fact that... But... Wait... Hmm. You're actually right, though. It really was the most delicious the very first time Paimon had it...

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: Then, you will find yourself craving something even more delicious. This cycle will repeat itself, time and again, simply because you seek to fill the void left by the memory of that very first bite.

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: And that void is precisely where countless desires and wicked deeds are born. But what if it worked the other way around? What if you could get that exact same feeling out of everything you eat, whenever you eat it, no matter how many times you've had it before?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, that sounds like some kinda dream world...

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: This is the world of Aurion, the world of tomorrow. In this world, no matter what you do, your heart shall always brim with that feeling, that sense of being touched at your very core. And of those feelings, love would be the most apparent of all...

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: It is a kind of love that can never be extinguished, a love that is unchanging and everlasting. And such a world, brimming with such eternal love, will become a realm free from worry and pain thereafter.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But it would also be a world where change is no more.

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: Yes. That is because... time and change are what ravage all things. Every second that passes is a second that erodes the everlastingness of love.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, what do you mean by "change is no more"?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It means whatever you eat, they will all end up tasting the same...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Hold on, how does that make any sense?!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah! So it's like... because everything you eat makes you feel super, super happy, it doesn't matter what you eat anymore?

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: That is right... You really are quite the clever little thing, Paimon.

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: The first step in shaping this world is to use the Shadow Realm... Light may soon cast its gaze toward the shadow, but that would still take some time...

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: We shall blanket the whole of Snezhnaya in the shadow realm, and then the entire world, so that all love may stand unchanging in a space with no beginning and no end... Thus shall we bring forth the Courtyard of Carefree Light.

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: Choice would lose meaning, while the difference between the chosen and unchosen will dissipate. In a world like this, I reckon even the Abyss would become lovable.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No way! Ugh...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Goggles said he wants to get his body back and go on all sorts of adventures with us! Goggles would never, ever want a world like this!

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: #No matter. There shall be a place for all of you in this carefree world — for {NICKNAME}, for Paimon, and even for the Proto-Man — whether you are willing or not.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's not a world I'm interested in either way...

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: A true pity. I thought this was something upon which we would share a common understanding. But that matters not, for the final understanding shall eventually come.

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: I assume this means you will now try to stop me... But I have no desire to raise my hand against you nevertheless. This, then, is my choice.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, you're not going anywhere!

choices.text: You're not looking at me, are you?

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: Hahaha! A most amusing notion. Your existence is such that none in this world can touch or diminish it.

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: Naturally, it follows that none in this world is able to assimilate or reforge you. That renders you a most unbefitting choice.

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: It's done. Now, all we have to do is... wait a little while longer...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wha... What is that? It's huge, and kinda weird, too...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, no, that's not the point!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're being so horrible, Aksinya! Just give us back Goggles!

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: Looks like the two of you are really fond of the Eye of Graeae... If only my former colleague was able to see the value of this creation as well.

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: ...Although the physical body has begun to transform, the consciousness has yet to take root... His Majesty...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah! This is...

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: This was the original body of the Tsar. But it would change into the form of a fae whenever speaking with us or traveling alongside other fae.

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: Unable to maintain his avatar after death, he reverted to his original state, a magnificent, almost transcendental form.

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: Have I ever told you this before? That the faces of the Proto-Man were actually modeled after the visage of His Majesty the Belyi Tsar's human manifestation?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Just give us back Goggles...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mmhmm! Paimon has zero interest in whatever you were babbling on about just now...

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: Very well. Here.

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: The Eye of Graeae was always built to host the Proto-Man's consciousness... Such that he would not disappear after offering his flesh and blood to His Majesty...

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: It was originally meant to preserve "him."

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: Now, since it is no longer useful to me, I shall therefore make a gift of it to you. I trust that you will find a good use for it.

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: #I hereby transfer its ownership to... {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...And Goggles?

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: Restored to original state. The {RUBY#[D]Eye of Graeae} is now at your service...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This isn't him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This isn't Goggles at all! This is just... a tool. It's nothing more than an empty shell!

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: I'm sorry. Its consciousness should already be part of the Primordial Human by now, to serve as the core of the Velikan {RUBY#[S]Svarod}of Light.

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: This is something I am unable to return to you. But don't worry, you will no longer grieve this soon, since...
...*sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: Because the Primordial Human has awoken.

dialogues.speaker: The Primordial One
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon... and Aksinya, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Goggles...?

dialogues.speaker: The Primordial One
dialogues.text: Yes, it is I... I now remember everything. Much time has passed... both for you, Aksinya, and for me.

dialogues.speaker: The Primordial One
dialogues.text: Fate truly is absurd. This is exactly the scenario that I strove to avoid when I was still in my prototypical form.

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: That's just how fate is. It pushes you to the cliff's edge, like the worst of nemeses.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A situation you had to avoid...?

dialogues.speaker: The Primordial One
dialogues.text: Yes, and that is why I tried to persuade Koshchei, Pavlina, and Alvis to stop her before she decided to begin the final experiment.

dialogues.speaker: The Primordial One
dialogues.text: After all, the authority that the Primordial Human wields may as well be a deadly{RUBY#[D]Ether} venom to humans and fae, who carry mixed desires within them...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait... So that blue algae thing, that Snegurochka, and the Domovoy Grand Duke from Novokitezhgrad... They betrayed Aksinya because of you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Awww!

dialogues.speaker: The Primordial One
dialogues.text: I promised them they could both stop Aksinya in and gain what they wanted in this way.

dialogues.speaker: The Primordial One
dialogues.text: Each of them was driven in their own way by ideals, or perhaps ambitions, that would see them transcend all life. This proved simple to use.

dialogues.speaker: The Primordial One
dialogues.text: By contrast, our dear Aksinya, our lovely Aksinya... The resolve she possessed seemed all the more unusual, did it not?

dialogues.speaker: The Primordial One
dialogues.text: And so, I incited them to divide me up, to split me into pieces, and to betray Aksinya...

dialogues.speaker: The Primordial One
dialogues.text: For if I were to become the Primordial Human, become a transcendent one... Just as I am now... That would mean that the world was about to undergo an inexorable revolution.

dialogues.speaker: The Primordial One
dialogues.text: The "beast" mocked me, for it believed its mission fulfilled. And I, despite fleeing my duties with all my mind, wound up here all the same.

choices.text: You don't want to become the Primordial Human.

response.speaker: The Primordial One
response.text: Yes, because... *sigh* Aksinya...

response.speaker: The Primordial One
response.text: You left no place for yourself in the world that would be born from these fresh schematics, did you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ehh!?

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: ...Yes. I am willing to believe in a nation of love everlasting. I believed in His Majesty the Tsar, and in his wish.

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: But those who have lost faith in love must be banished from the new world, the realm of eternal love. I do not have the right to enter that world.

response.speaker: The Primordial One
response.text: Banishment? It is more akin to being slain, I rate. Eternal love, eternal overflow, eternal joy... Those who trust not to love and joy cannot enter this realm.

response.speaker: The Primordial One
response.text: But it is precisely one who does not trust either who could fashion such a cruel plan. This, the "loving" Belyi Tsar had long realized.

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: And that is why he is great. He chose me. This is my duty, my sole purpose for living. Even if I cannot step into the new world...

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: I wish to see its descent with my own eyes, to see it rise from a cornerstone forged from my corpse.

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: ...And as for you? Do you still believe that an eternity of love can be attained without His Majesty's plan?

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: Alvis, Koshschei, and Pavlina... Their pursuits have melted away like snow... None can resist the erosion of time, the withering of the spirit, the shriveling of dreams.

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: So many have given up so much in the fight to keep a joyous spirit... But none have succeeded.

response.speaker: Aksinya
response.text: What choice can you make at this point?

response.speaker: The Primordial One
response.text: None. You know this as well, Aksinya, that I could not refuse you once I had recalled all, what more, now that I have become the Primordial Human.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, Goggles... Are you really gonna open the gate to the Courtyard of Carefree Light?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Might there be another choice?

response.speaker: The Primordial One
response.text: You have my utmost thanks, you two, for giving me the chance to give up even at this stage.

response.speaker: The Primordial One
response.text: But... Alas, I cannot let her plans come to naught. So, if you wish not to see this come to pass... Please, stop both of us.

response.speaker: The Primordial One
response.text: #But before that, {NICKNAME}, I would like to show Aksinya something... I'd like you to answer a question of mine.

response.speaker: The Primordial One
response.text: #You seek your sibling, and you have traveled the world to understand {M#her}{F#him}, to seek the things that you missed out experiencing alongside {M#her}{F#him}, to stand before {M#her}{F#him}.

response.speaker: The Primordial One
response.text: #But if the gap between you is too great, and you, in the end, find that {M#she}{F#he} is not what you imagined, that your once-beloved kin is kin no longer...

response.speaker: The Primordial One
response.text: #That {M#she}{F#he} has changed and become another person, someone you never imagined {M#she}{F#he} might...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #What!? Why would that ever happen? {NICKNAME}'s {M#sister}{F#brother} wouldn't change!

response.speaker: The Primordial One
response.text: This is but a hypothetical scenario. Do not be alarmed, Paimon.

response.speaker: The Primordial One
response.text: #What would you do, {NICKNAME}? I'd... like to know your answer.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #If {M#she}{F#he} changes...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #Then I will learn to love {M#her}{F#him} once again...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: No matter how many times I have to do it.

response.speaker: The Primordial One
response.text: #Thank you, {NICKNAME}. That was wonderful. Better by far than any answer I imagined I would get.

response.speaker: The Primordial One
response.text: The time has come, and the Courtyard shall soon activate. It is a shame...

response.speaker: The Primordial One
response.text: "But what's to be done? Whomsoever loves should share the burden of destiny with the ones he loves."

choices.text: You don't wish to create a new world...

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: ...At the end of the day, I haven't been able to do anything in time...

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: Ah, what a shame... This was the sole great endeavor I was meant to undertake...

dialogues.speaker: The Primordial One
dialogues.text: As I see it, you have done enough... You endured the passage of time for so long, even in such a place.

dialogues.speaker: The Primordial One
dialogues.text: Your ambition burned so strongly that even the branches of fate had to bend low for you... To the point where you could escape from this place.

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: In truth, my escape from the Shadow Realm was largely thanks to Izmaylov's aid. He said it was the last thing he could do for me.

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: And yet, I still failed... and lost everything... and where are we falling to now?

dialogues.speaker: The Primordial One
dialogues.text: Perhaps we shall fall into the endless depths of the Shadow Realm, tumbling for five hundred years, and another five thereafter.

dialogues.speaker: The Primordial One
dialogues.text: But this is already the best possible ending I could face.

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: Okay?

dialogues.speaker: The Primordial One
dialogues.text: Yes, Aksinya. Here, there is no "His Majesty, the Belyi Tsar." No "Primordial Human." Here, there is no court jester of Snezhnaya, no Snegurochka, no other fae.

dialogues.speaker: The Primordial One
dialogues.text: Here, there is only you and me. Here... we do not even need names.

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: Is this what you wanted?

dialogues.speaker: The Primordial One
dialogues.text: ...Yes, it is indeed. This is good — to be within this shadowy realm, a world as small as a walnut shell. Just the two of us, at the very end.

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: ...I once thought that I could never be worthy of setting foot in a world like this...

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: #...You know, {NICKNAME} is right. Why should we fear love's fading, that we should insist that it stand eternally?

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: One who dares to believe in love will not be obsessed with its disappearance... and if I believe in it, so what if I should lose it?

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: I'd climb back up, shake the dust and dirt free, head off in pursuit once more, to take hold, to go forth, to love again!

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: Why did I... Why did I want to...

dialogues.speaker: The Primordial One
dialogues.text: Aksinya...

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: *sigh* ...I once hated this world, imprisoned as it was within an eggshell. Yet in the end, all I did was build another shell.

dialogues.speaker: The Primordial One
dialogues.text: Perhaps that is just how fate has been from the start, pushing you to the cliff's edge, like the worst of nemeses.

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: Heh. Never thought you'd be the one to say that to me.

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: ...I was once driven to such fury when I learned the truth of the world, and bearing that indignation, I asked the Tsar:

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: "What is the point of an egg that does not allow the life within it to emerge from the shell? Why does it exist in this universe at all?"

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: But I never received the answer I wished to have from him.

dialogues.speaker: The Primordial One
dialogues.text: So that was a thought you once had. I see.

dialogues.speaker: The Primordial One
dialogues.text: What about now, Aksinya? Do you still think this way? You've done so much... Did you ever find an answer to that question?

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: More or less, I suppose. The answer is... *sigh* Y—You already know the answer, don't you?

dialogues.speaker: The Primordial One
dialogues.text: ...You once considered me far too selfish.

dialogues.speaker: The Primordial One
dialogues.text: But no matter what form love takes, whether it gives or takes possession, outward expressions of love always reflect what lies within in some way.

dialogues.speaker: The Primordial One
dialogues.text: To love the world is to love yourself...

dialogues.speaker: The Primordial One
dialogues.text: But this is also a great thing, because this is how the world is, and one's desire to be saved must be strong enough to save the world entire.

dialogues.speaker: The Primordial One
dialogues.text: I'd always believed that I should love myself first, and then the world, or I would fall into error, just as I have today.

dialogues.speaker: The Primordial One
dialogues.text: But you... you are truly magnificent, Aksinya.

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: ...A cheap compliment.

dialogues.speaker: The Primordial One
dialogues.text: Ah, I am hurt. That came from the bottom of my heart.

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: Hmph...

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: Yes. Everything... Pavlina, Koshchei, Alvis, you... and... and His Majesty the Tsar... all the things you wanted...

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: Why am I only now realizing that I, too... once longed for those things...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oof, finally! We've finally made it out of that Shadow Realm!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hang on, Paimon doesn't see Goggles or Aksinya... and the Belyi Tsar's body is missing, too. Where have they gone to?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I don't think we'll ever see them again...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. Do you think it's possible that Goggles might actually be hiding inside that mechanism Aksinya gave you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You know how it's like in those shows? They make you think that someone's vanished forever, and then, POOF! They pop up right in front of you again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How about you let Paimon take a look?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: And so, Paimon makes several attempts at "cracking" the mechanism.\nBut the only voice that answers is a cold, lifeless one.\nThis is how the two of you learn that while "Goggles" has retained some of its abilities, it really is nothing more than, well, a pair of goggles at this point.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He's... really fallen into that deep, deep hole...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But that's his own fault for choosing to open the door to that Courtyard of Carefree Light or whatever... But... Paimon thinks he was pretty cool when he chose to help Aksinya.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Heh, even if one day the whole world were to turn against you, Paimon would stand by you no matter what!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And I'll do the same for you, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm.. You know, now that the Belyi Tsar's body has gone missing... We're gonna be in big trouble if someone sees us now!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've got to get out of here, fast!
